  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],

    "The 'Combined' paradigm has a sample size approximately 4.3 times larger than 'Dim Visual Only' and nearly 14.7 times larger than 'Sham', which may influence statistical power if group means differ.",
    "The 'Sham' paradigm has the smallest sample size (n=3,505), followed closely by 'Bright Visual Only' (n=3,323), requiring caution when interpreting differences involving these groups due to lower statistical power.",
    "The 'ICMS Only' group (n=11,378) is intermediate in size but significantly smaller than the 'Combined' group, potentially obscuring subtle effects of ICMS stimulation compared to the baseline or combined conditions."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The analysis reveals a robust dataset suitable for comparing navigation efficacy across stimulation conditions. The high success rate (~73%) and moderate path efficiency (~0.47) suggest that while most mice reach the target, the path taken is often inefficient. The substantial sample size for the 'Combined' condition allows for more reliable estimation of its performance profile compared to the 'Sham' and 'Bright Visual Only' conditions. However, without specific group-by-variable means or statistical test results (e.g., ANOVA, t-tests) in the provided artifacts, definitive claims regarding which specific paradigm outperforms others for specific metrics cannot be confirmed; only the descriptive distribution and sample sizes can be reported.",
  "limitations": [
    "The provided artifacts contain only global summary statistics (mean, sd, min, max) and row counts; they do not contain group-specific means, standard errors, or p-values required to determine significant differences between the five paradigms.",
    "The large disparity in sample sizes across groups (ranging from 3,323 to 48,846) may introduce bias if the smaller groups (Sham, Bright Visual Only) exhibit different variances or distributions not captured by the global summary.",
    "No temporal or individual mouse-level data is provided to assess consistency of performance within specific paradigms or to control for mouse ID as a random effect."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Compute group-specific descriptive statistics (mean, sd, n) for each of the five stimulation paradigms across all five response variables to enable direct comparison. Subsequently, perform one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis tests for each response variable to identify significant differences between paradigms, followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons with correction for multiple testing."
}
